dish.title: Palestinian Musakhan: Sumac Chicken and Onions on Flatbread
dish.description: Boneless chicken thighs rubbed with sumac, allspice, and cardamom and roasted, then piled with a heap of onions slowly cooked in olive oil and sumac onto taboon-style flatbreads and baked until the edges crisp, finished with parsley and lemon.

recipe_version.title: Palestinian Musakhan: Sumac Chicken and Onions on Flatbread
recipe_version.description: Boneless chicken thighs rubbed with sumac, allspice, and cardamom and roasted, then piled with a heap of onions slowly cooked in olive oil and sumac onto taboon-style flatbreads and baked until the edges crisp, finished with parsley and lemon.

ingredients.name: flatbreads
ingredients.display_name: 8-inch taboon-style or pocketless pita flatbreads whose label lists wheat flour, water, yeast, salt, and sugar

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Preheat the oven to 425 F. Toss the chicken with 2 tbsp sumac, the allspice, cardamom, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp oil and spread on a sheet pan. Thinly slice the onions, chop the parsley, and cut the lemon.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.body: Roast the chicken until browned at the edges and 175 F, about 22 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips. Leave the oven on.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.body: While the chicken roasts (overlap stated): warm 1/2 cup oil in the 12-inch skillet over medium-low, add the onions and 1 tsp salt, and cook, stirring often, until very soft and sweet but not browned, about 25 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp sumac.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.body: Lay 2 flatbreads on each sheet pan. Spread the onions and their oil over the breads and top with the chicken. Bake until the bread edges crisp, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Scatter parsley, cut each flatbread in quarters on the cutting board, and serve with lemon wedges.

Compared with lebanese-baked-kibbeh: sumac chicken on bread, not a bulgur and lamb bake. Compared with roasted-cauliflower-shawarma-plate: a sumac-onion flatbread, not a shawarma-spiced vegetable plate.
